Box gives triangular f*f → 2/3 (p0001 confirms). A Gaussian bumps this to 1/√2≈0.707. Sparse delta-combs likely give (2-1/k)/3≤2/3, i.e. worse. So the real lever is a smooth single bump plus direct height optimization. I will put a general randomized height-improver in the deepen slot starting from a Gaussian seed, and use the two explores to scan parametric bump families to learn which shape is extremal.

beliefs.statement: f*f is always symmetric about the center of f's support. agenda.question: Can a genuinely different, low-dimensional construction — f as a mixture of 3-6 free smooth bumps (~3K parameters) globally optimized in parameter space — reach the competitive region (>=0.85) and open a new line?
agenda.plan: From scratch: parametrize f as a sum of K=3..6 Gaussian/raised-cosine bumps with free centers, widths, amplitudes; optimize by random multi-start + parameter-space coordinate descent (and Nelder-Mead if scipy helps) on R; upsample the best to N=800 and run block ascent + restarts. If it reaches >=0.85, branch and polish it; else record the low-dim family's ceiling.
agenda.why: All current lines descend from the same height-vector/tiny-N recipe; a low-dimensional parametric family is a genuinely different region and cheap to search.

experiments.if_gain: Keep the best, refine the dip schedule (more dents, wider amplitude range) and adopt peak-dip as a standard stage.
experiments.if_not: Record that peak-dip is a minor lever on this basin and shift the thread to restart/upscale schedule only.
